title: Item base
description: An item base, per docs/10-items.md. The base determines class, footprint, mass, attachment slots and the class-specific numbers; affixes, condition and attachments are rolled or accumulated on top of it at generation. Adding a weapon is a data edit.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. Permanent once shipped.

extends.description: Id of another item base to inherit from.

name.description: Display name, before the tier and affixes decorate it.

description.description: One sentence about what this is, shown on the inventory sheet's inspect pane and nowhere else. Prose, never a number: what a thing does is a sentence and how well it is doing it is a word (docs/01 clause 4), so a description carrying a digit is a content bug the INVENTORY gate refuses. Optional -- SimItems.description_of falls back to a sentence built from the class and the equip slot, so a new base is never blank.

appearance.description: What this looks like lying on the ground. Omit it and the renderer draws the generic ground-item diamond, which is the normal state until art exists.

attachmentSprite.description: The picture drawn on the pawn when this part is fitted to a held weapon. Unlike every other overlay in the pipeline it does not share the hand anchor -- a suppressor hangs off a muzzle, and a pistol's muzzle and a rifle's are rows apart on the 32x40 canvas -- so it is drawn once and moved to wherever the *host* says that slot is. See `partAnchors` on the weapon.

partAnchors.description: Where this weapon keeps each of its attachment slots, in pawn-canvas pixels off the body rect, keyed by slot name. Read by presentation/appearance.gd when a fitted part declares an `attachmentSprite`; a slot with no anchor draws its part at the body's own origin. Only the held weapon needs these, and only for slots something is drawn for.

sprite.description: Registry key resolved to assets/sprites/<key>.png by presentation/appearance.gd. A key, not a path, so content stays engine-agnostic.

tint.description: Colour for the procedural fallback, and a modulate over the sprite when one exists.

equipSprite.description: A different picture from `sprite`: what this looks like worn or held on a body, not lying on the ground. Authored on the same feet-anchored pawn canvas as the body it will be drawn over (32x40; presentation/appearance.gd's PAWN_KEYS and assets/sprites/README.md), so the renderer composites it at the identical rect with no per-item offset math and mirrors it with the body. Read only when this base occupies an equipment slot presentation.gd renders (currently back, primary, secondary); other slots leave it declared but unused until a body-part anchor exists for them.

equipSpriteFront.description: An optional second picture, always drawn over the body regardless of which slot `equipSprite` itself draws under. For a worn item whose straps cross in front of the torso -- a backpack, a chest rig -- `equipSprite` is the bulk of the item behind the body and this is just the strap/buckle piece in front of it. Same canvas convention as `equipSprite`. Omit it for anything that doesn't need a front piece; most equipment won't.

class.description: What the item is. Affixes declare the classes they can roll on via appliesTo, and equip slots accept by class.

size.description: Footprint in inventory cells, unrotated. One cell is about a fist -- a bandage is 1x1 and a fire axe 1x4 (docs/10-items.md#inventory-space-and-weight).

massKg.description: Mass of one unit, empty. A container's contents are counted on top of this, recursively. Never shown to the player as a number.

bandageTier.description: What grade of dressing this item makes when it is used to bandage a wound, per docs/05-health-injury.md. Absent means the item cannot dress a wound at all. A flat scalar, not a nested block: the content validator is shallow, so a nested object would get an is-it-an-object check and nothing more -- this way the enum is actually enforced.

cleanTier.description: What grade of clean this item buys when it is spent on the `clean` verb, per docs/05-health-injury.md's "whether it was cleaned" sepsis factor. Absent means the item cannot clean a wound at all. Ranked worst-first here and best-first in SimTreatment.CLEAN_ORDER, which is the pick order when an actor carries more than one. A flat scalar for the same reason bandageTier is one: the content validator is shallow, so an enum on a top-level key is actually enforced.

closeKind.description: How this item closes a wound when it is spent on the `close` verb. Absent means it cannot close one. Which closer a wound wants is the wound kind's own `closeKind` in SimWounds.WOUND_KINDS: a `suture` holds a cut, bite or burn shut and a `splint` holds a fracture still. The two are matched exactly, never ranked -- a suture kit does not close a fracture and a splint does not close a cut.

stack.description: How many units share one footprint. 1 means the item does not stack.

equipSlot.description: Which equipment slot this base can occupy, if any. Wearing a container is what grants its grid (docs/10-items.md#what-you-can-carry-is-what-you-chose-to-wear).

container.description: Grid this item provides when it is a container. Present on packs, rigs and pouches; absent on everything else.

melee.description: The four properties docs/09-combat.md says a melee weapon has. Read by the melee module when this base is equipped to the primary slot.

light.description: What this base lights, per docs/03-attention.md#light. Read by the light module when the base is equipped to a hand slot. Magnitude is reach in metres, in the same metres as every other channel -- there is no brightness unit.

magnitude.description: Reach in metres. The values are docs/03's table -- candle 3, campfire 20, lamp 35, floodlight 90 -- and a test pins them against LIGHT_TABLE so the two cannot drift.

slots.description: Attachment slot names, per docs/10-items.md#attachment-slots. Attachments move freely between compatible bases.

requiredSlots.description: Slots this base cannot work without, a subset of `slots`. An empty one blocks the weapon: SimAttachments.blocked_reason puts a reason on the built profile and SimRanged._idle_weapon, SimMelee.try_begin_swing and npc_combat._ranged_range all read it, so a pistol with no barrel refuses to fire and an NPC holding one does not walk into range of it. The subset claim is a gate lane, not a schema rule -- nothing here can see the sibling key.

defaultParts.description: The parts this base comes assembled with, keyed by slot name and naming an attachment base. SimAttachments.assemble fits them when the item spawns, so the template is the receiver and the weapon in the world is an assembly -- pull the barrel out and what is left is a frame. Every slot named here must be one this base declares in `slots`, every value must be an attachment that fits that slot, and the graph must not cycle; check_m2_attach.gd's ASSEMBLE and CYCLE lanes judge all three, because the validator will not look inside this object. A base's own massKg is the receiver alone: the parts weigh what they weigh and item_mass_kg counts them.

attachment.description: Present on an attachment base and absent on everything else, per docs/10-items.md#attachment-slots. `fits` is the set of host slot names this will go into -- a list rather than one name, because 'moves freely between compatible bases' is the point of the mechanism. The `melee` and `ranged` tables are multipliers folded over the host weapon's own profile by sim/modules/attachments.gd, keyed by the profile field they scale, so an attachment declares what it multiplies and nothing has to know what an optic is. The content validator is shallow and will not look inside this, which is what godot/check_m2_attach.gd is for.

fits.description: Host slot names this attachment is compatible with.

melee.description: Multipliers over the melee profile, keyed by field: damage, reachMetres, staggerTicks, speed.

ranged.description: Multipliers over the ranged profile, keyed by field: damage, noise, flash, magSize, reloadTicks, rangeMetres, cone, handling. `handling` scales how fast the weapon comes up and settles, against its content-declared `weight`. `cone` scales the felt aim cone, so a number above 1 is an accuracy cost -- docs/09 charges one for a suppressor.

fieldSwap.description: Whether a person can change this part with their hands, away from a gunsmithing bench. A magazine, a sight, a can on a thread: yes. A barrel, an action, an axe head: no. Absent means no, which is the safe default -- a part nobody has thought about is bench-only rather than silently field-swappable. Read by sim/modules/gunsmith.gd on the item.attach / item.detach commands, never inside SimAttachments.attach itself.

overrides.description: Profile fields this part *replaces* rather than scales, per kind, against sim/modules/attachments.gd's OVERRIDABLE whitelist. A multiplier cannot express a caliber, so `ammo` and `jams` are the narrow exception to "multipliers, never adders". Resolved by agreement, not by order: one distinct value wins however many parts declare it, and two distinct values block the weapon outright -- a conversion barrel and a cylinder that take different rounds make a gun nobody can load. Only `ranged` exists; a `melee` key would be a socket nothing reads.

ranged.description: Replacement values keyed by profile field: `ammo` (an item base id) and `jams` (a boolean).

structural.description: Whether the host is made of this part rather than merely carrying it. A structural part's own condition drags the whole assembly down -- SimItems.assembly_condition takes the worst of the host and its structural parts -- which is what makes swapping a worn barrel for a good one a repair. An optic or a suppressor is not structural: as it wears it simply does less, per effect_scale. A part may be structural and still declare multipliers; a long barrel is both.

wearsOn.description: What wears this part, from sim/modules/attachments.gd's WEAR_EVENTS vocabulary: shot, reload, hit, jam. A part declaring none never wears. The words are a code-owned list rather than an enum here because the registry is the authority and check_m2_attach.gd asserts both directions -- every word declared is one the module knows, and every word the module knows is declared by something shipped.

wearRate.description: Multiplies SimAttachments.PART_WEAR_PER_EVENT for this part. Above 1 is docs/10's "suppressors wear out fast"; below 1 is a part that outlives the weapon.

armor.description: Coverage per body part 0..1. Read by infection transmission (docs/10-items.md#129) — max coverage applies, absent is 0.

ranged.description: Optional ranged block. Every field is optional except `weight` -- see its own description.

weight.description: How much weapon there is to bring up, mirroring melee.weight. Multiplies every rung of docs/09-combat.md's raise -> steady -> fire -> recover ladder through sim/combat.gd's raise_ticks / steady_ticks / shot_recover_ticks, so a submachine gun is quick to the shoulder and a crossbow is not. Required for the same reason it is required on melee: a weapon with no declared heft would silently borrow 1.0 and handle like a service pistol.

jams.description: Whether this weapon can jam as it degrades, per docs/09-combat.md: "degraded firearms jam, and clearing a jam takes longer than a reload". Firearms only -- a bow has nothing to stovepipe -- which is why it is declared here rather than inferred from having a magazine. The chance itself is not authored: SimItems.JAM_CHANCE_BY_BAND derives it from condition, so it cannot drift from the band the inventory screen shows for the same weapon.

food.description: Present on anything edible. docs/12-resources.md#content-shape puts spoilage rules in JSON alongside loot tables, and docs/04-survival-needs.md is where the numbers come from: "quality matters, not just quantity: raw and spoiled food fills the bar but damages mood and carries illness risk; cooked meals restore more and give a mood bonus". Presence of this block is what makes an item food -- SimNeeds.is_food asks nothing else.

hunger.description: Hunger restored, on the 0..100 need scale.

mood.description: Mood applied on eating. Negative for raw, positive for cooked; a spoiled item overrides it with SimNeeds.SPOILED_MOOD regardless of what is declared here.

spoilDays.description: In-game days before it goes off. 0 means it keeps indefinitely, which is what canned means.

illnessChance.description: Chance per meal of a bout of food poisoning. Multiplied by SimNeeds.SPOILED_ILLNESS_MUL when the item has actually spoiled, so one authored number moves both cases together. The `iron_stomach` trait is full immunity rather than a reduction.

drink.description: Present on anything drinkable; presence is what makes an item a drink -- SimNeeds.is_drink asks nothing else, exactly as is_food asks only for `food`. `thirst` is the plain half (a water bottle drinks +50, the number SimNeeds.drink used to carry as a literal). The other three keys are docs/04-survival-needs.md's stimulant clause -- "no caffeine-style hard reset; stimulants exist as rare loot with a real crash afterward" -- made content: `rest` is the lift, paid now into the rest pool, and `crashRest` is taken back out of the same pool `crashAfterTicks` later. SimNeeds.drink_spec judges the block whole: a lift declared without both crash keys is refused as not drinkable at all rather than drunk for free, because the validator does not recurse and a free stimulant is exactly the wrong number nothing would report. What is left in the hand afterwards is the top-level `empties`, not a key here, so a fuel can can say the same thing.

thirst.description: Thirst restored, on the 0..100 need scale.

rest.description: Rest restored on drinking -- the lift. Omit for anything that is not a stimulant.

crashRest.description: Rest drained when the lift wears off -- the crash. Author it at or above `rest`: a stimulant is a loan, not a gift. A second can inside one lift adds its crash to the pending one and pushes the clock out, so chaining defers the crash and makes it bigger; the pool floors at zero, and an empty pool is the existing passed-out crisis, which is what "a real crash" means here.

crashAfterTicks.description: Ticks from drinking to the crash (12000 to the in-game hour).

mood.description: Mood applied on drinking, on the meal-mood clock -- SimNeeds.MEAL_MOOD_SOURCE, replaced rather than stacked, wearing off with MEAL_MOOD_TICKS. Absent means the drink says nothing about mood.

illnessChance.description: Chance per drink of a bout of illness -- docs/04-survival-needs.md's "untreated water carries illness". The same bout `food.illnessChance` rolls, on the same stream, with the same `iron_stomach` immunity. Absent means the drink is clean; the well fills bottles with `item.water.bottle.untreated`, which carries it, and boiling at a lit campfire turns one into `item.water.bottle`, which does not. SimNeeds.drink_spec refuses a value outside 0..1 outright, because the validator does not recurse.

fuel.description: Present on a fuel can. `litres` is what the can holds, and a can is poured whole: SimVehicles pours min(litres, room in the tank) and the rest is spilt. Not a running count on the instance -- an item instance carries a condition, a stack count and an affix list, and a can that remembered its litres would need a fourth per-instance number, a mass that moves with it (`massKg` is a constant of one unit), a fill word for the can, and a HUD clause for that word. Whole cans keep all four out. Refused into anything but an engine: a battery wants the charger docs/23 names in what's left, and a bicycle has nothing to fill. What is left afterwards is the top-level `empties`.

litres.description: Litres tipped into a tank when the can is poured. A sedan holds 40, a van 60, a truck 80 (content/vehicles), so a 10 L can is a quarter of a sedan -- a find, not a fill.

empties.description: The base left in your hands once one unit of this is spent -- the bottle without the water, the can without the fuel. Read by SimNeeds._consume_item, the one place a unit is spent (a drink, a wash, a wound cleaned with the bottle, a can poured), so every spend leaves the same thing. Stowed where the spent unit was; dropped at the feet when nothing has room. A flat scalar at the top level for the reason bandageTier is one: the content validator is shallow, and a string with a pattern up here is actually enforced. Absent means nothing is left -- a crushed can is not worth carrying.

modification.description: Present on a modification consumable, per docs/11-crafting.md#content-shape: "a modification consumable declares which operation it performs and against which item classes". Adding a consumable is a data edit provided the operation it names already exists; adding an operation is an entry in SimModification.OPERATIONS. That registry is code because an operation is behaviour, and check_mods.gd is what asserts every declared operation is in it -- no schema can.

operation.description: The operation this consumable performs. Must name an entry in SimModification.OPERATIONS. Not an enum here: the registry is the authority and a duplicated list would drift from it.

appliesTo.description: Item classes this consumable may be used on. An empty list is not allowed -- a consumable that applies to nothing is a content mistake, not a universal one.
